topics.flagship-ru-ua: A six-day ceasefire in Russian-occupied Oleshky in southern Ukraine has held for its first 30 hours, according to officials (4 sources). Trump says a Putin-Zelensky meeting to end the war will happen 'very soon' (3 sources). Drones reportedly hit another container ship off Bulgaria, and Türkiye, Bulgaria and Romania held a security meeting in Sofia on Oct. 28 over the Black Sea attacks. Norway and Finland also reportedly held a rare phone call with Putin.
topics.flagship-ir-il: Trump says the Iran war will end 'when I want it to', as a report says costs have reached $47 billion (2 sources). Two outlets report that US forces in the region are restocking munitions and readying aircraft for renewed strikes on Iran. Houthi attacks on a Saudi refinery pushed oil prices up (1 source), Yemeni officials are appealing for help as the Houthis tighten the siege of Taiz, and one outlet (Drop Site News) reports that the UAE is secretly assisting the Houthis.
topics.T15: India is evacuating tens of thousands ahead of 'very severe' Cyclone Arnab, which is due to make landfall Wednesday, with about 400,000 people needing evacuation (3 sources). Other items are minor and single-source: flooding on the Nepal Rasuwagadhi–Bhotekoshi corridor, supermarket hoarding in the UK after a 'Be Ready' campaign, and earthquake-related stories from China and Venezuela.
topics.T01: Jordanian air strikes in southern Syria killed at least seven people, including three children (3 sources). Pakistan rejected Afghan Taliban claims about cross-border shelling at Angoor Adda in South Waziristan that killed a civilian (4 sources). The remaining items are single-source commentary on global war preparedness, Turkey-Greece Aegean politics and US retrenchment from Europe.
topics.T02: Coverage is sparse and mostly generic. Items include a report on persecution of Christians, aid commissioning at Nigerian IDP camps, and a reported Swiss suspension of MSF funding over sexual-misconduct allegations in Chad. None of these is corroborated by multiple outlets.
topics.T03: An Illinois man, Matthew Unglesbee, is accused of mailing letters containing white substances to Congress (2 sources). He reportedly told the FBI the powder was salt and that it was a joke.
topics.T04: The Ebola outbreak in the DRC has passed 10,000 cases after a nurse was killed and another injured, making it the second-largest Ebola outbreak globally and the fastest-growing in DRC history (2 sources). Kenya released 20 contacts of its first Bundibugyo case from quarantine, and Nigeria is paying contacts of its confirmed case for quarantine compliance. Other items: a bird flu outbreak at a Utah mink farm, a Newcastle disease outbreak in Brazil poultry with South Africa imposing only targeted curbs, and rising dengue in southern Brazil.
topics.T05: Coverage is sparse and consists of opinion pieces on Russian influence in Africa, 'Islamo-leftism' and regime-change operations. There is no concrete coup or instability event.
topics.T06: Youth-driven unrest continues across Europe, led by large-scale riots in France that remain tense despite crackdowns (multiple sources). Spanish police admitted they underestimated the violence in Barcelona, and 19 people were arrested in Bilbao. Commentary is raising questions about spillover to Germany and elsewhere.
topics.T07: The head of the UN nuclear agency said there is no indication Iran has tried to repair or rebuild nuclear facilities damaged in US and Israeli strikes this year or last (3 sources).
topics.T08: Coverage is a scattering of unrelated items. In Nigeria, three people were killed in Kebbi violence and troops foiled an ambush in Zamfara. Other items cover a reported foiled Flydubai hijacking attempt, an Arakan Army relocation plan on the Bangladesh-Myanmar border, and commentary on Russia in Africa. The Jordan strikes in Syria are covered under Military Conflict.
topics.T10: India is reportedly working with Sarvam AI on a battlefield AI framework and approved about $22 billion in military spending. Russia released footage of a Bulava submarine-launched ballistic missile test, and Germany is weighing its next fighter jet partnerships. Rajnath Singh met US War Secretary Hegseth at the ASEAN defence ministers' meeting in the Philippines.
topics.T11: The US and Japan conducted a coordinated anti-ship strike during Exercise Keen Sword 27. British and Norwegian F-35s escorted a B-52 during STRATCOM's Exercise Global Thunder, and the India-Singapore SIMBEX-2026 naval exercise concluded (2 sources). US Southern Command and Colombia will begin the Southern Vanguard exercise with 800 troops on November 2.
topics.T12: Multiple corporate cyber incidents were reported. Hackers are probing a newly patched critical Oracle E-Business Suite flaw (CVSS 9.8; 2 sources), UNM Health's ransomware attack disrupted patient care, and Japan's GMO told customers to disconnect PCs after a breach. Other reports cover Coinbase customer data exposed via a vendor breach, 123 Reg disclosing an 'AI cyberattack' with a suspected China nexus, and commentary on AI-enabled attacks. Most items are single-source.
topics.T13: Coverage is sparse and unrelated. Items include an EU proposal to give its border agency deportation powers, 180 Nigerians returned from Libya, vehicle arson in Ceuta, and US immigration politics in New York.
topics.T14: Israel's Foreign Ministry confirmed an attempted terrorist attack near the Israeli Embassy in Belgrade (5 sources). The US expelled a Cuban diplomat after a confrontation at the UN with Ambassador Mike Waltz, and a French deputy chief of mission in Tehran was reportedly intimidated by suspected Iranian security agents.
topics.T16: Brazilian presidential loser Flávio Bolsonaro has not conceded and is calling for the election to be annulled. His whereabouts are unclear after Brazil cancelled his passports and Argentina said he flew to Ecuador (5 sources). Israel's election appears tight, with exit polls showing Netanyahu's bloc and Eisenkot's bloc each on about 51 seats (4 sources). Later projections give Netanyahu's bloc 54 seats and Eisenkot's 47, with neither holding a majority (2 sources). A hacker reportedly targeted the US Federal Election Commission website.

bluf: Jordanian air strikes in southern Syria killed at least seven people, including three children, according to three outlets. Brazil's defeated presidential candidate Flávio Bolsonaro has not conceded and is calling for the election to be annulled, and his whereabouts are unclear after Brazil cancelled his passports and Argentina said he flew to Ecuador. The Ebola outbreak in the DRC has passed 10,000 cases after a nurse was killed and another injured, making it the second-largest Ebola outbreak globally and the fastest-growing in the DRC's history. A six-day ceasefire in Russian-occupied Oleshky, Ukraine, has held for its first 30 hours, per officials, while Trump says a Putin-Zelensky meeting will happen 'very soon'. India is evacuating tens of thousands ahead of the 'very severe' Cyclone Arnab, which is due to make landfall Wednesday and puts about 400,000 people in need of evacuation. Israel's Foreign Ministry confirmed an attempted terrorist attack near the Israeli Embassy in Belgrade, reported by five outlets. In Israel's election, projections give Netanyahu's bloc 54 seats and Eisenkot's 47, with neither holding a majority.
